after: ## Why Akhirah is a key belief
alt: Qur’an 3:185 above three consequences of belief in the Last Day: accountability, so Muslims act well when unobserved; justice, so wrongs will be put right; and perspective, so wealth and status are not chased.
caption: This world is a test and the next is permanent: three consequences follow.

alt: Five numbered stages: death at the decreed time, when the Angel of Death takes the soul; Barzakh, the barrier between death and resurrection; resurrection when Israfil (AS) blows the trumpet; the Day of Judgement with the book of deeds and scales; and Jannah or Jahannam.
caption: Barzakh comes before resurrection and is temporary; final judgement follows.

alt: According to the Hadith, two angels often named Munkar and Nakir ask the dead three questions: who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is the man sent to you. A believer answers and the grave becomes peaceful; a disbeliever cannot answer. Barzakh is a foretaste, not the final outcome.
caption: Barzakh is a foretaste of reward or punishment, not the final judgement.

alt: Five features of the Day of Judgement with Qur’anic references: the book of deeds given in the right or left hand, the scales of justice, nothing too small to count, the body as witness, and Allah’s mercy with the Prophet’s (pbuh) intercession.
caption: Judgement is complete and just, and mercy is greater than anger.

alt: Seven rituals in order with why each matters: Qur’an and the Shahadah near death, closing the eyes and covering the body, ghusl, the white kafan, Salat al-Janazah, burial facing the Qiblah, and mourning, including the widow’s iddah of four months and ten days.
caption: Each ritual expresses a belief: Tawhid, purity, equality or community.

alt: A table of differences in death rituals: four takbirs for Sunni and five for Shi’a Muslims in the Janazah prayer; how openly grief is shown; gatherings on set days in some South Asian communities seen by others as custom; differing views on visiting graves; A note covers cremation, delays and martyrs.
caption: Show at least one difference and explain what it reveals.

alt: A Hadith in Sahih Muslim: when a person dies their deeds end except for three, ongoing charity, knowledge that benefits others and a righteous child who prays for them, which is why Muslims build wells, fund schools and pray for their parents.
caption: This Hadith explains why Muslims build wells, fund schools and pray for parents.
